note: CODE DERIVATION: data/silva_2023_ecohis.py melts xlsx columns ECOHIS1..ECOHIS13 and lowercases them (number-preserving rename, ecohisN = source column ECOHISN); no labels in the file tie N to wording, so text is tied via the paper's Table 2 numbering itN (paper_explicit) and verified by route 1 (all 13 per-item mean/median/SD/skew/kurtosis/min/max profiles match their own row only; see verify_silva_2023_ecohis.R). TEXT: item_text is Table 2's English verbatim with the 'itN. ' prefix stripped (curly apostrophes kept). ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE: the study used the Brazilian Portuguese version of Tesch, Oliveira & Leao (2008); the deposit and supplements hold no Portuguese item wording (xlsx: no variable or value labels for ECOHIS columns; rmd: only Portuguese code comments, no items; article: English only), so text_source=translated_substitute with the authors' own English (translation_source=study_supplied), language=Portuguese, _translated columns empty. Note Silva's English renders stems as 'Has your child ever ...' where the canonical English reads 'How often has your child ...'; shipped as the study printed it. Instructions: none printed by the study; left blank (Pahel 2007's canonical English instructions not substituted). OPTIONS LEFT BLANK, deliberately: the paper says only 'Responses are given in a 5-point Likert type scale' and prints no anchors. The canonical ECOHIS (Pahel 2007, printed form) has SIX options, '1. Never, 2. Hardly ever, 3. Occasionally, 4. Often, 5. Very often and 6. Don't know', so one of six is absent from the 1..5 data and which one is not established. The authors treat 5 as the top level (the xlsx SCORE column equals the mean of all 13 codes to 5e-7, and Table 2 reports max 5), but the response data argue otherwise: pooled over items, respondents choosing 1/2/3/4/5 have mean dmft (ceod) 0.92/2.41/2.89/3.81/2.71 and mean rest-score (other items, 5s excluded) 1.25/1.65/1.88/2.50/1.88, i.e. level 5 sits at level 3, not above 4; item-rest r averages 0.567 with 5 kept vs 0.576 with 5 set missing; and 25/371 respondents (6.7%) use a 5, close to Pahel's '<7 percent' Don't-know rate. That is consistent with code 5 being 'Don't know' rather than 'Very often', but n=38 cells is small, so no anchor was attached to any code. RIGHTS: originator Pahel, Rozier & Slade (2007) published the full instrument in a CC BY article; no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause located (two web searches for ECOHIS terms of use/permission, 2026-09-10); Silva 2023 is CC BY 4.0. Silence, so extracted; no register row written (rounds may not write ship rows). MINOR SOURCE DEFECTS: Table 2 prints it13 skewness 2.50 where the data give 2.470 (all other it13 stats reproduce), and it8 kurtosis 6.52 where the data give 6.529.
public_note: The study describes its ECOHIS as a 5-point scale and prints no anchor labels, but the published ECOHIS has six options including "Don't know", and in these data code 5 behaves like a non-ordinal answer (respondents choosing 5 have lower caries counts and lower scores on the other items than those choosing 4), so option_text is left blank and resp 5 should not be assumed to mean "Very often"; item wording is the authors' English rendering of the Brazilian Portuguese version they administered
